brief: Wedbush (Outperform, PT $345 vs. $173.73) addresses reports that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after NYT, WSJ and Bloomberg reporting of a second relationship with a direct report and a hired executive-search firm; Wedbush does not call the ouster certain but sees it as the likely outcome. An executive transition would raise uncertainty, but Wedbush argues NVDA's valuation (~10X FY'28 EPS versus a typical 20-30X+ range for semis with ~70% margins and ~70% growth) and near-term setup (a 5%+ beat streak, supply locked through 2027-2028, demand outrunning supply, Rubin Vera near launch) give the company room to find its footing. Historical precedents are mixed: Marvell's 2016 ouster eventually led to AI-ASIC success, while HP's and Intel's abrupt post-affair transitions preceded lasting decline, though those CEOs weren't founders. Apple's Jobs-to-Cook handoff, the closest parallel, worked despite differing skill sets. If NVDA stumbles, Wedbush names AMD, then Cerebras, as the likeliest beneficiaries, since Google's TPUs can't be a primary third-party supplier and custom ASICs remain hard to execute. Wedbush also flags a reported US policy restricting Chinese firms' access to high-end accelerators outside China as a modest, non-primary revenue risk.
